title: Territory operational tactics and simulated failure notes
content:
Purpose:
Notes and tactical playbook for running operator-facing drills when region-pinning enforcement is toggled/modified. This is a working doc: mix of checklist, lab script, escalation wording for legal/contract handoff, and postmortem triggers.

Context + assumptions:
- Focus: mid-size tenants (10k-100k monthly requests) that opt into hard region pins (edge->region anchor).
- We will exercise 3 main failure modes: routing mismatch -> transient cross-region spill, pin config rollback, and anchor eviction due to capacity enforcement.
- Tests are staged in the region-staging catalog (us-east-2, europe-west-1).
- Network and KMS constraints simulated via the sandbox proxy (see confluence:residency-sim-lab-2025).

Quick runbook (operator shorthand):
1) PRE-CHECK (T-30m)
   - Verify tenant pin state: /admin/tenants/{id}/region-pin -> expected region and TTL.
   - Telemetry health: ensure residency-metrics exporter up (grafana panel "residency-heartbeats").
   - Confirm canary group size: 2% traffic by header flag X-Geo-Test:true.
   - Slack channel ready: #residency-ops (notify: @oncall-sre, @account-eng).

2) ENABLE ENFORCEMENT (T0)
   - Flip feature flag: residency.enforcement = strict -> set for tenant id in staging.
   - Add temporary routing rule: routeFallbackTier=local-first.
   - Start live sample: set X-Geo-Test true for canary clients.

3) MONITOR (T+0..T+30m)
   - Primary signals (alert if any):
     * cross_region_rate > 0.5% for pinned tenant (from residency-telemetry).
     * error_rate_pinning > 0.2% OR latency_95 > baseline+150ms.
     * KV-cache-miss ratio increases by > 10% within 5m (indicates charged cold-starts).
   - If any signal breaches: pause enforcement (toggle to graceful) and escalate.

4) ROLLBACK PATHS
   - Graceful fallback: residency.enforcement = soft -> allow cross-region for existing sessions for 5 minutes, observe.
   - Immediate rollback: restore previous routing policy from snapshot route-policy@{timestamp}.
   - If rollback fails: fail open to hosted cluster (route to neutral model variant).

5) POST ACTIONS (T+1h)
   - Export sampling for tenant: collect 10k request traces and KV-eviction logs.
   - Run fuzzy compare vs baseline eval set (script: tools/residency/diff_eval.sh).
   - Populate incident stub: PD-8321 if operator action required.

Operator crib notes (things we learned / must remember):
- KV cache warming is the scariest silent failure. If enforcement causes sudden cold-key churn, latency and token-cost both spike. When in doubt, favor soft enforcement first.
- Customer-visible errors often occur when the auth/KMS key is region-locked and we attempt a cross-region fallback. Add explicit preflight check for key policy.
- Surge contractors (3rd-party proxy teams) will need a 1hr handoff briefing; include contact + minimal command list in handoff email.

Contractor handoff template (short):
- Subject: "[HANDOFF] Residency enforcement drill - Tenant {id} - {date}"
- Body bullets:
  * Tenant + tenant-id + expected pinned region
  * Flags set: residency.enforcement -> strict / canary header X-Geo-Test:true
  * Key contacts: Amira Patel (eng), Jonas Keller (sre), LegalOps - legal-ops@redwood.com
  * Quick rollback commands: <1> set residency.enforcement=soft; <2> route-policy restore {snapshot}
  * Evidence to gather: sample traces, KV eviction table, KMS denied logs

Simulated-failure matrix (for tabletop):
- Scenario A: "Partial dataplane partition" -> simulate 10–30s loss to europe-west-1
  * Expected: traffic for pinned tenants should pause, fallback path should serve neutral model in region.
  * Probe: injector sim-loss-eu.sh (10s) -> watch cross_region_rate + errors
- Scenario B: "KMS policy deny during fallback" -> simulate KMS deny on fallback cluster
  * Expected: fail-open to hosted neutral (must not leak customer data).
  * Check: audit log contains KMS_DENY and tenant request bodies redacted.
- Scenario C: "Anchor eviction due to capacity" -> simulate node drain in pinned region
  * Expected: canary batch should be rerouted to secondary pinned region or soft fallback. Monitor billing tag change.

Telemetry gating and SLOs for drills:
- Before flip: capture baseline windows for 1h.
- Drill SLOs (targets):
  * cross_region_rate < 0.5% during 30m window
  * latency_95 increase < 120ms
  * errors attributable to pinning < 0.1% of requests
- If any SLO violated, create incident and mark drill as failed.

Open decisions / TODOs:
- [ ] Decide canonical naming for snapshots (route-policy@{env}-{ts} vs rp-{tenant}-{ts}) -> ops prefers rp-{tenant}-{ts}.
- [ ] Add KMS-policy preflight in the SDK path; where to place quick-check? client-sdk vs gateway? (assign to ENG-4510).
- [ ] Confirm legal's minimal evidence set required for enterprise audit when we exercise enforcement (ask LegalOps).
- [ ] Run cross-region chaos test with 50 tenants simultaneously to understand cascading KV eviction costs. (blocked by capacity reservation).

Post-drill notes template (fill after run):
- Run id, operator, time window
- What breached (telemetry + attached graphs)
- Actions taken and timestamps for each toggle
- Customer visible impact (if any) and comms sent (copy of message)
- Lessons learned (short)
- Follow-ups (owner + ETA)

Commands quick-list (for handoff email):
- set-enforcement soft: POST /admin/flags residency.enforcement=soft --tenant {id}
- restore-route-policy: POST /admin/routes/restore {snapshot_id}
- sample-extract: python tools/residency/sample_extract.py --tenant {id} --limit 10000 --out /tmp/{id}-sample.json

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Avoid toggling enforcement during heavy maintenance windows (esp. DB schema upgrades).
- Make runbooks idempotent and include expected success metric so contractors can signal checkpoint completion.
- We should add an automated sanity-check that scans for tenant KMS key region mismatch BEFORE enforcement flips. If mismatch -> abort and create PD automatically.

References and quick links:
- residency-sim-lab-2025 (confluence) -> lab config for injectors
- PD-8321 -> incident template for drills
- ENG-4510 -> KMS preflight epic
- PR: inference-runtime#789 -> small routing fix used in the canary

Questions for next sync with LegalOps and SalesEng:
- What constitutes "sufficient evidence" of region adherence for EU audits? (raw traces vs hashed evidence?)
- When a large customer requests a soft->hard enforcement change, what is the minimum notice window Sales must provide? (T-72h?)

Last notes: this doc is deliberately tactical — split the polished playbook into a longer "operator-runbook" doc once we stabilize the checklist. For now, use this as the canonical sandbox-run notes and attach the telemetry snapshots after each run.

-- Amira (notes)
